# Introduction

Most Standardised MedDRA Queries (SMQs) are "simple": a term belongs to the
query as soon as it is part of the narrow or the broad search. These can be
derived in a single `derive_vars_query()` call, as shown in the
[OCCDS vignette](occds.html).

A handful of SMQs are **algorithmic**. For these, the broad search terms are
split into categories and a term only counts towards the query if it occurs
*together with* a term from another category. Whether a record contributes
therefore depends on the other records of the same subject, which is something
`derive_vars_query()` cannot express on its own.

This article shows how to derive such a query in two steps:

1. Use `create_query_data()` and `derive_vars_query()` to add one query
   variable per algorithm category. Keeping one variable per category in the
   dataset makes the derivation traceable --- a reviewer can see exactly which
   term contributed which category.
1. Use `derive_var_joined_exist_flag()` to look across the records of a subject
   and flag the terms which contribute to the algorithm.

## The example algorithm

We use *Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)* as the example. Its algorithm combines the
narrow search with four categories of broad terms:

| Category | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Narrow | Core anaphylactic reaction terms |
| A | Broad terms specific enough to qualify on their own |
| B | Upper airway / respiratory |
| C | Angioedema / urticaria / pruritus / flush |
| D | Cardiovascular / hypotension |

A term contributes if it is

* a **narrow** term, or a term from **category A**; or
* a term from **category B** occurring together with a term from **category
  C** (and vice versa); or
* a term from **category D** occurring together with a term from **category B**
  or **category C** (and vice versa).

i.e. `A or (B and C) or (D and (B or C))`.

# Set up the Queries Dataset {#queries}

The terms of an SMQ are read from the MedDRA dictionary by a company-specific
function passed to the `get_terms_fun` argument of `create_query_data()` ---
admiral does not provide one, as the database layout is company-specific. See
`create_query_data()` for the interface this function has to implement.

An algorithmic SMQ needs one addition to that function: it must be able to
return the terms of a **single algorithm category**. No admiral-side change is
required for this, because `basket_select()` accepts any number of *named*
arguments through its `...` argument and passes them on unchanged. Requesting
`basket_select(..., algorithm_category = "B")` therefore makes
`basket_select$algorithm_category` available inside your `get_terms()`
function, where it can be used to subset the terms of the SMQ.

**Note**: *MedDRA is a licensed dictionary, so the examples below run against a
small made-up term list rather than the real SMQ.*

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Stand-in for the company MedDRA database and get_terms() function, so that
# this article can be run. Not shown to the reader.
smq_anaphylaxis_db <- tribble(
  ~TERMCHAR,                  ~SCOPE,   ~ALGCAT,
  "ANAPHYLACTIC REACTION",    "NARROW", NA,
  "ANAPHYLACTIC SHOCK",       "NARROW", NA,
  "ANAPHYLACTOID REACTION",   "NARROW", NA,
  "CIRCULATORY COLLAPSE",     "BROAD",  "A",
  "SHOCK",                    "BROAD",  "A",
  "BRONCHOSPASM",             "BROAD",  "B",
  "DYSPNOEA",                 "BROAD",  "B",
  "STRIDOR",                  "BROAD",  "B",
  "WHEEZING",                 "BROAD",  "B",
  "ANGIOEDEMA",               "BROAD",  "C",
  "FLUSHING",                 "BROAD",  "C",
  "PRURITUS",                 "BROAD",  "C",
  "URTICARIA",                "BROAD",  "C",
  "BLOOD PRESSURE DECREASED", "BROAD",  "D",
  "HYPOTENSION",              "BROAD",  "D",
  "TACHYCARDIA",              "BROAD",  "D"
)

get_terms <- function(basket_select, version, keep_id, temp_env) {
  terms <- smq_anaphylaxis_db

  # a narrow search returns the narrow terms only, a broad search returns all
  # terms of the SMQ
  if (basket_select$scope == "NARROW") {
    terms <- filter(terms, SCOPE == "NARROW")
  }

  # `algorithm_category` is passed in via the `...` argument of
  # `basket_select()` and restricts the terms to one algorithm category
  if (!is.null(basket_select$algorithm_category)) {
    terms <- filter(terms, !is.na(ALGCAT) & ALGCAT == basket_select$algorithm_category)
  }

  out <- transmute(
    terms,
    SRCVAR = "AEDECOD",
    TERMCHAR,
    GRPNAME = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)"
  )
  if (keep_id) {
    out <- mutate(out, GRPID = 20000021L)
  }
  out
}
```

Each part of the algorithm is defined by its own `query()` object:

* `SMQ01` and `SMQ02` are the standard narrow and broad searches of the SMQ.
  They create `SMQ01NAM`, `SMQ01CD`, `SMQ01SC`, `SMQ01SCN` and their `SMQ02`
  counterparts, and the algorithm is applied on top of them.
* `CQ01` to `CQ04` are the four algorithm categories.

The categories are defined as *customized queries based on a basket*, i.e. the
`basket_select()` object is wrapped in a `list()`. That way only `CQzzNAM` is
created for them --- a plain `basket_select()` would additionally populate
`SCOPE`, giving non-standard `CQzzSC` variables which add nothing here, as the
scope is already captured by `SMQ01SC`/`SMQ02SC`.

```{r}
anaphylaxis_queries <- list(
  query(
    prefix = "SMQ01",
    name = auto,
    id = auto,
    add_scope_num = TRUE,
    definition = basket_select(
      name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
      scope = "NARROW",
      type = "smq"
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "SMQ02",
    name = auto,
    id = auto,
    add_scope_num = TRUE,
    definition = basket_select(
      name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
      scope = "BROAD",
      type = "smq"
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ01",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category A",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "A"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ02",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category B (upper airway/respiratory)",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "B"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ03",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category C (angioedema/urticaria/pruritus/flush)",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "C"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ04",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category D (cardiovascular/hypotension)",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "D"
      )
    )
  )
)

queries_anaphylaxis <- create_query_data(
  queries = anaphylaxis_queries,
  get_terms_fun = get_terms,
  version = "29.1"
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(queries_anaphylaxis)
```

# Example Input Data {#input}

```{r}
adae <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID, ~AESEQ, ~ASTDT,       ~AEDECOD,
  "01",     1,      "2021-03-05", "Anaphylactic reaction",
  "01",     2,      "2021-05-12", "Headache",
  "02",     1,      "2021-02-11", "Circulatory collapse",
  "03",     1,      "2021-04-02", "Dyspnoea",
  "03",     2,      "2021-04-02", "Urticaria",
  "04",     1,      "2021-06-18", "Hypotension",
  "04",     2,      "2021-06-18", "Wheezing",
  "05",     1,      "2021-07-21", "Hypotension",
  "06",     1,      "2021-08-03", "Urticaria",
  "06",     2,      "2021-08-04", "Pruritus",
  "07",     1,      "2021-09-09", "Nausea",
  "08",     1,      "2021-01-05", "Dyspnoea",
  "08",     2,      "2021-06-20", "Urticaria"
) %>%
  mutate(ASTDT = ymd(ASTDT))
```

# Step 1: Derive One Query Variable per Algorithm Category {#step1}

A single `derive_vars_query()` call derives all prefixes at once.

```{r}
adae_query <- adae %>%
  derive_vars_query(dataset_queries = queries_anaphylaxis)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_query,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, SMQ01NAM, SMQ02NAM,
    CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM
  )
)
```

Note that none of these variables on their own answers whether a term
contributes to the algorithm: subject `03` has a category B term (`CQ02NAM`) on
one record and a category C term (`CQ03NAM`) on another, and subject `05` has a
category D term with nothing to combine it with.

# Step 2: Flag the Contributing Terms {#step2}

Whether a record contributes depends on the other records of the same subject,
so each record needs to "see" them. This is what the joined functions do: with
`join_type = "all"` each record of the input dataset is joined with **all**
records of the same subject, and the variables listed in `join_vars` are made
available for the joined record with a `.join` suffix. The current record's own
variables are available unsuffixed.

As the result is a simple yes/no per record, `derive_var_joined_exist_flag()`
is used --- it adds the single flag specified by `new_var` and sets it to `"Y"`
for every record which has at least one partner record satisfying the
condition.

`filter_join` then spells out the algorithm as a condition on the record pair.
A record contributes if it is a narrow or category A term on its own, or if a
partner record supplies the missing half of one of the other combinations. Note
that the pairing is symmetric: both the category B and the category C term of a
B+C combination have to be flagged, which is why each combination appears twice
in the condition.

The MedDRA algorithm is defined at case level, but in practice a study will
usually also require the combined terms to occur close to each other in time.
Here the contributing terms have to start within 7 days of each other. Since
`join_type = "all"` also joins a record with itself, the same window condition
can be applied to the narrow and category A branches without excluding them.

```{r}
adae_alg <- adae_query %>%
  derive_var_joined_exist_flag(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    new_var = ANAPTFL,
    join_vars = exprs(ASTDT, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join = abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 &
      (
        # a narrow term or a category A term contributes on its own
        !is.na(SMQ01NAM) | !is.na(CQ01NAM) |
          # category B together with category C
          (!is.na(CQ02NAM) & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) |
          (!is.na(CQ03NAM) & !is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) |
          # category D together with category B or category C
          (!is.na(CQ04NAM) & (!is.na(CQ02NAM.join) | !is.na(CQ03NAM.join))) |
          ((!is.na(CQ02NAM) | !is.na(CQ03NAM)) & !is.na(CQ04NAM.join))
      )
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, ASTDT, AEDECOD, SMQ01NAM, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM,
    CQ04NAM, ANAPTFL
  )
)
```

`ANAPTFL` cannot be derived from the queries dataset, as it does not depend on
the reported term alone but on which terms occur together.

Walking through the subjects:

* `01` --- *Anaphylactic reaction* is a narrow term and contributes on its own.
  The unrelated *Headache* is not flagged.
* `02` --- *Circulatory collapse* is a category A term and contributes on its
  own.
* `03` --- *Dyspnoea* (B) and *Urticaria* (C) occur on the same day, so both
  contribute.
* `04` --- *Hypotension* (D) and *Wheezing* (B) occur on the same day, so both
  contribute.
* `05` --- a category D term with no category B or C term, so nothing
  contributes.
* `06` --- two category C terms, which is not a qualifying combination.
* `07` --- not part of the SMQ at all.
* `08` --- a category B and a category C term, but more than 7 days apart, so
  neither contributes.
